title: Almeda v. Court of Appeals
summary: The Supreme Court discussed the requirements and effects of adoption under the Domestic Adoption Act. Adoption creates a relationship of parent and child between the adopter and the adopted, and severs the parental authority of the biological parents.
doctrine: Adoption severs all legal ties between the biological parents and the adopted child, except in cases of succession rights to the biological parents. The adopted child is considered the legitimate child of the adopter for all intents and purposes. The best interest of the child is the paramount consideration in adoption proceedings.
fullText:
GARCIA, J.:

This case involves a petition for adoption under the Domestic Adoption Act of 1998, Republic Act No. 8552.

Adoption is a juridical act which creates between two persons a relationship similar to that which results from legitimate paternity and filiation. The adopted child is considered the legitimate child of the adopter for all intents and purposes.

The paramount consideration in adoption cases is the best interest of the child. The court must be satisfied that the adoption will redound to the best interest of the child and will provide a home and support that the child needs.
